body: Possible NPE. `getValueFrom()` is null for any env var that has neither `value` nor `valueFrom`, for example an env var with no value that comes from a user-supplied unsupported pod template. Before this change the EnvVar was compared directly and this could not fail. Because the call is in a `filter` inside `envVars`, the whole reconcile would throw. Null-check `getValueFrom()` before calling `getSecretKeyRef()`.

Only the secret *name* is compared, so changing `secretKeyRef.key` (same secret, different key) is not detected and no upgrade/rollout decision is made. Other `valueFrom` sources (configMapKeyRef, fieldRef, resourceFieldRef) are now dropped by the filter, so changes to them are ignored as well. The old code compared the full EnvVar. Compare name+key, or keep comparing `valueFrom` as a whole.

Sorting args before comparing hides changes that depend on order. The first arg is the command (`start`, `--optimized`...), and repeated or positional options can have order-dependent meaning. Also, `getArgs()` can be null or empty depending on the pod template. If the goal is to ignore how the operator orders the options it generates, make the generator deterministic rather than sorting here.

The docs say the Operator will fail when `rolling-updates` is not enabled, but nothing in the operator checks this. `UpgradeLogicFactory`/`UpdateSpec.findUpdateStrategy` never look at `spec.features`, so `update.strategy` is applied whether or not the feature is on. Either add the check (for example, set a status condition or error when an update strategy is set without the feature) or fix the documentation.

This changes a public exit-code contract. `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` goes from 4 to 3, and 4 is reused to mean 'feature disabled'. A script or operator written for the previous behaviour will read exit code 4 as 'recreate needed' when it now means 'feature disabled'. If the codes must change, call it out explicitly (release notes/upgrade notes). Also make sure 3 does not collide with other exit paths of this command.

The feature check runs before `validateConfig()` and the `--file` checks, and it uses whatever profile is resolved at that moment. With an optimized/built server whose build did not enable the feature, `--features=rolling-updates` passed to this command may be rejected as a build-time option change, or may not be reflected in `Profile`. Please confirm that `Profile` is initialized from the CLI args of this command at this point. Otherwise users can't enable the feature on the command line as the docs suggest (`kc.adoc` appends `--features=rolling-updates`).

Unrelated to rolling updates, and a security regression: this PR removes the check `DeviceGrantType.isDeviceCodeDeniedForDeviceVerificationFlow`. Without it, a device code that the user already denied can still continue through the consent flow and have consent granted. The corresponding tests in `OAuth2DeviceAuthorizationGrantTest` are deleted too. This looks like an accidental revert from a bad rebase or merge and should be dropped from the PR.

Unrelated revert of the `force-login` option of the reset-credential-email authenticator (`isConfigurable()` now returns false and `getConfigProperties()` returns null). Realms that already configured `force-login=true` will silently stop forcing re-login after a password reset, which is a security behaviour change. The docs, release notes and `ResetPasswordTest` coverage are removed as well. It also brings back a wildcard import `org.keycloak.models.*`. This should not be part of a rolling-updates PR.

Unrelated revert: the OpenAPI `@APIResponses` for 201/204 are removed from the group create endpoint, and the admin UI message keys are changed. These look like leftovers from a bad rebase. Please drop the unrelated changes from this PR.
The docs now say exit code 4 means 'feature disabled', but it used to mean 'recreate upgrade'. Please add an explicit upgrade note that the exit codes changed, so anyone who scripted against 4 knows.
